items.review_rationale: Reviewed the finite diagonal-sum trace of n-by-n matrix over field K with positive size n; distinguished this linear-algebra trace from trace in a field extension.

references.context: Array of n rows and n columns with entries a_ij in the field K.
Entries whose row index equals column index in a square matrix.

references.phrase: finite sum of n diagonal entries
references.context: Field sum indexed by i from 1 through n, yielding an element of K.

references.disposition: Trace of a matrix here is not itself the trace of an element of a field extension.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed affine hull as all finite nonempty affine combinations of S subset R^d with coefficients summing to one; preserved empty S convention and fixed dimension d>=1.

references.context: Linear combination of finitely many vectors x_i in S with scalar coefficients summing to one.
Sum of the real coefficients of an affine combination equals one; coefficients need not be nonnegative.
Dimension d and number k of participating points at least one.

references.phrase: affine hull of empty set is empty
references.disposition: With k>=1, S empty produces no combinations; this source explicitly permits empty affine hull.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed affine hull as intersection of all affine-combination-closed supersets of S, including empty affine-closed set and arbitrarily many supersets; not equated with convex hull.

references.phrase: subsets S and C of R^d

references.context: Subset closed under all finite affine combinations with real coefficients summing to one, without a nonnegativity constraint.
Meet of the family of all affine-closed subsets C containing S, yielding least affine-closed superset.
Sum of finitely many scalar-weighted vectors with scalar coefficients totaling one.

references.disposition: Universal closure requirement is vacuous for an empty set; preserves the explicit empty-hull convention.

items.review_rationale: Read independent-events probability product rule on one probability space for two measurable sets, allowing zero probabilities and requiring intersection probability equality.

references.context: Set consisting of sample points lying in both measurable events.
Product of probabilities of two events on the same normalized probability space.
Independence holds exactly when intersection probability equals product of the two marginal event probabilities.

references.disposition: No positivity or conditional-probability division hypothesis is needed for the defining product rule.
